description: AOT warning baseline for Excalibur.Dispatch. Only warnings with documented justification may be added. PRs adding entries require explicit justification.
policy: EVERY entry below is third-party. None is ours. The population was taken from the mirror's own AOT Publish Validation report -- 208 warnings, 0 errors, publish SUCCEEDED -- and parsed with the same attribution the validator uses: 0 of 208 were attributed to an Excalibur assembly. The bar on OUR code is therefore unchanged and still zero. An entry matches on code AND package AND a substring naming the specific member whose reflection could not be proven safe, so a warning from our code, or a DIFFERENT warning from the same dependency, cannot match one of these and will still fail the gate. Do NOT add a wildcard or a package-wide entry: that would delete the only property that makes this file safe to keep. Proven before landing by re-applying the validator's own predicate to the real report: 208 of 208 absorbed, while a synthetic Excalibur-owned warning and a synthetic same-package-different-member warning both stayed unmatched, and no entry carries a substring short enough to act as a wildcard.

warnings.justification: Dapper 2.x maps result rows by reflection, which cannot be proven safe by the trimmer. The AOT-safe alternative is the source-generated Dapper.AOT, which is a substrate change against a dependency this project mandates and needs its own ruling before adoption.

It deliberately does not suppress IL2026 inside the shipped library, on the stated grounds that a suppression there would hide the risk from the consuming application. No consumer-side action remains.
